TATAMOTORS.note: Oct 2025 demerger: each Tata Motors share became 1 TMPV (passenger vehicles, same ISIN) + 1 TMCV (commercial vehicles).

GUJGASLTD.note: Jul 2026: renamed Gujarat Energy (GUJENERGY); demerger gave 1 GSPL Transmission share per 3 held.

JBCHEPHARM.note: Jul 2026: merged into Torrent Pharmaceuticals, 51 Torrent shares per 100 JB Chemicals shares.

GRAPHITEOLD.note: Jun 2002: old Graphite India Ltd (BSE 509590) merged into Carbon Everflow, now Graphite India (GRAPHITE), 14 new shares per 10 old.

TATAMETALI.note: Feb 2024: Tata Metaliks (BSE 513434) merged into Tata Steel, 79 Tata Steel shares per 10 Tata Metaliks shares.

VIKRANTTYR.note: 2003: Vikrant Tyres (BSE 509301) merged into JK Industries (now JK Tyre), 9 JK shares per 20 Vikrant shares; price is per pre-2014-split JK share (the site applies the 2014 split to quantity).

GUJGASOLD.note: 2015: old Gujarat Gas Company (BSE 523477) merged 1:1 into Gujarat Gas Ltd (GUJGASLTD); priced like GUJGASLTD (rename + 2026 GTL demerger). The site applies the 2019 split to quantity.

ZANDUPHARM.note: Zandu Pharmaceutical Works (BSE 506720): 2009 FMCG demerger gave 14 Emami shares per Zandu share (84 after Emami's 2010 split and 2013/2018 bonuses); Zandu Realty merged into Emami Infrastructure (now Emami Realty) in 2018, 7 shares per share.

GSKCONS.note: Apr 2020: GlaxoSmithKline Consumer Healthcare (BSE 500676) merged into Hindustan Unilever, 439 HUL shares per 100 GSKCH shares.

RANBAXY.note: 2015: Ranbaxy Laboratories (BSE 500359) merged into Sun Pharma, 4 Sun shares per 5 Ranbaxy shares.

TATACOFFEE.note: Jan 2024: Tata Coffee (BSE 532301) merged into Tata Consumer Products, 3 TCPL shares per 10 Tata Coffee shares.

ITCBHADRA.note: 2002: ITC Bhadrachalam Paperboards (BSE 500340) merged into ITC, 1 ITC share per 16; 45/16 after ITC's 2005 split and 2005/2010/2016 bonuses.

STERLITE.note: Aug 2013: Sterlite Industries (BSE 500900) merged into Sesa Goa (now Vedanta), 3 shares per 5.

INDAL.note: Mar 2005: Indian Aluminium (BSE 500445) merged into Hindalco, 1 share per 7; 10/7 after Hindalco's 2005 split.
